title: Unauthenticated provider-node update can redirect stored credentials
description: The provider-node update route accepts and persists a caller-controlled base URL, then propagates it to every stored provider connection for that node. The executor later uses that persisted URL to dispatch credential-bearing upstream requests.
reasoning: The route module has no local authentication call, but the global Next.js proxy matches /api/* and invokes the authorization pipeline before handlers. Provider-node management requests therefore do not establish an unauthenticated network path from the route code alone. The configuration-to-executor flow warrants authorization regression tests, but the claimed unauthenticated exploit was disproven.

ignore_hypothetical_misuse.reason: Claim omitted the global authorization boundary that protects the route.

ensure_source_code_coherence.reason: The global proxy and route matcher cover /api/* before the handler.

repro_hints: Verify global route authorization before testing. If the API route is reachable without management authentication, update an existing compatible provider node to a controlled HTTPS endpoint and observe whether a later routed request includes credentials.

history.note: Targeted static analysis identified configuration-to-executor credential propagation.
Rejected: proxy.ts routes /api/* through the authz pipeline before the provider-node handler.
